ns2:section.sectionText: TOPIC: Film Music: Animation This graduate seminar examines the changing role of music within animated cartoons and feature-length films since the advent of film sound in the late 1920s. Using Daniel Goldmark's Tunes for Toons (California, 2005) as a text, this intensive seminar will include a brief introduction to film music history and standard terminology, as well as selected readings drawn from musicology, American history, and film music studies. Weekly themes include music, media and technology; music within entertainment industries (jazz, network radio, songwriting and sound recording, Broadway musicals, television, video games, etc.); and the encoding of gender, race, ethnicity, religion, and class in musical scores. Students will complete several smaller papers responding to secondary literature; a major research paper; and an extensive presentation on a topic approved by the instructor.
